Name: William Weir
Question: What would happen if both presidential candidates died on Election Day?
Answer: The election proceeds as if they were both alive. When the votes are tallied, we will have elected a President (who is dead) and a Vice President (who is alive). In a literal Constitutional approach, on Inauguration Day, the Vice President-elect is sworn in as Vice President, and as there is a vacancy for the office of President, is then sworn in as President. Practically I think we would skip their swearing in as the Vice President and just swear them in as President without objection, although I think we would have to officially declare them to be Vice President prior to them taking the oath of office as President.
